title: AngleMeasurement
description: An angle with an EXPLICIT unit, before conversion to canonical radians. The unit is mandatory: a bare number is ambiguous, and guessing 'probably degrees' is exactly the class of mistake that puts a 45-radian rotation into a Blender scene. This is an INPUT-boundary shape only. Once interpreted, an angle travels as a plain number of radians in a named field (rotation_euler_radians, desired_after_radians), so an AngleMeasurement never reaches the worker — the same discipline that keeps Measurement out of a Job payload. Direction of rotation is carried by the SIGN of the value, so an operation never needs a separate direction token. JSON cannot encode NaN/Infinity; the finite rule is enforced by the validation layer (studio_spatial.angles), which reports INVALID_UNITS. Note what is absent: no axis field. An axis belongs to the OPERATION that rotates something, not to the measurement of an angle.

value.description: Magnitude in the given unit. May be negative (rotation about the axis in the negative direction) and is deliberately NOT reduced modulo a full turn: 720 degrees is a legitimate two-turn instruction, and collapsing it to 0 would destroy intent. Conversion and normalization are different concerns.
